title: Greek Fire — the ancient weapon we lost the recipe to
voiceover: In the 7th century, the Byzantine Empire invented a weapon so terrifying that even today we don't know exactly how it worked. It was called Greek Fire. A liquid that burned on water. Stuck to ships. Couldn't be extinguished. Ignited on contact. For 800 years it saved Constantinople from invasion after invasion. The recipe was the empire's most guarded secret. Only a handful of families knew it. They died one by one without writing it down. We have descriptions. We have theories. The actual formula is lost. The most powerful weapon in the medieval world is just gone. Follow Mindbloom for one fact a day.
